name: clear_problems
description:
Clear stale persisted problems for the current project so a fixed file
stops blocking the Stop hook.

Problems are cleared per-source-per-file as validators re-run: a run only
clears problems for the files it re-checks. So when you fix a file but a
later run doesn't re-check that exact path, its old problem lingers and the
Stop hook keeps blocking on it even though the code is correct.

Use this tool when you have verified a reported problem is stale — the
underlying file is fixed and the failure no longer reproduces — but the
Stop hook keeps replaying it.

- Pass `file_paths` to clear only those files' problems (preferred: targeted,
  won't wipe unrelated findings).
- Omit `file_paths` to clear ALL persisted problems for the project (blunt
  reset — use when the whole stored set is stale).

This only clears the *stored* problem records the Stop hook reads; it does
not modify code or re-run analysis. If the problem is real, it will be
re-recorded on the next validation run.

file_paths.description: Project-relative file paths whose stale problems should be cleared. Omit to clear ALL persisted problems for the project.

name: list_problems
description:
The findings behind the alert, for the agent that wants them.

`Hooks.AnalysisAlert` puts a count and an age on every tool call and stops
there — a finding list on every call is noise the model learns to skip, which
costs the signal a second time and more permanently than never sending it. So
the alert pushes the fact and this pulls the detail, and the split only works
because asking is one tool call.

## Paginated, and not optionally

This working copy holds over 400 credo findings. An unpaginated list would
overflow the tool-response window for the same reason the alert is counts-only
— and a tool that dies on a large project is one nobody can rely on when a
project gets large, which is exactly when they need it.

Defaults to the first page and to `error` severity, because the common case is
"what is blocking me" rather than "everything anyone has ever noticed".

Scoped to the working copy, like everything else keyed on the harness: these
are the findings from *this* checkout's analyzers, not the project's.

severity.description: Filter by severity — `error`, `warning` or `info`. Omit for all.
